description: Mark an existing memory as useful (D77): record that it demonstrably paid off. Call it ONLY on an explicit signal — the user confirmed it helped ('that was the one', 'saved me again'), or your completed/accepted work clearly relied on that memory and the user saw the result. NEVER call it because a memory appeared in memory_search results, a memory_list inventory, or the session-start block: passive exposure never refreshes usefulness. Exposure is counted automatically under retrieved_count; the useful buckets increment only through this tool, a human approval at review, or a supersede. Useful is split automatically: useful_self for personal memories and unpublished project drafts (the author's own utility), useful_team for approved/published project memories (team knowledge reused) — pass kind only to override. Returns the cumulative counts and reuse_rate (useful / retrieved). The counters live in the local SQLite index, not in the Markdown source of truth, and never leave this machine.

id.description: ID of the memory being confirmed useful (memory_search / memory_list return ids).

kind.description: Which useful counter. Default: auto — personal memories and unpublished project drafts count useful_self; approved/published project memories count useful_team. Pass only to override the auto split.

name: memory_useful
